requirements.description: For every compact simple gauge group G
requirements.location: Section 4, printed p.6; section 1 defines gauge-group convention
requirements.gap: Classical G-valued link multiplication and gauge-invariant holonomy conjugacy classes are now kernel-checked. Compact simple group quantification is defined, but the quantum theory is not yet identified with these G-dependent observables.

requirements.description: Full four-dimensional R^4, not only a cutoff, torus or lower-dimensional model
requirements.gap: QFT data live on four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, but Yang–Mills existence there is not proved.

requirements.description: Axioms at least as strong as the Wightman or Osterwalder–Schrader schemes [45,35]
requirements.gap: A concrete Wightman-style schema exists but its adequacy relative to [45,35] has not been independently established; no candidate existence proof.

requirements.description: The quantum fields construct pure Yang–Mills for the specified gauge group and curvature action
requirements.gap: A genuinely G-dependent four-dimensional lattice action is kernel-checked, but its character weight, Haar measure, continuum limit and connection to Q's actual Wightman quantum correlations have not been established. A formal negative theorem proves that adding these classical checks without connecting them to Q leaves the unrelated-massive-QFT loophole open. Identification remains MISSING, never 'partial' by label alone.

requirements.description: Local quantum operators corresponding to gauge-invariant polynomials in F and its covariant derivatives
requirements.gap: Classical curvature-jet trace polynomials and nonlocal G-valued lattice holonomy conjugacy classes are defined, with concrete gauge-invariance proofs for the latter. Local gauge invariance of curvature expressions, renormalized field matching, and the full operator algebra remain missing.

requirements.description: Operator renormalization and dimension ≤ d filtration; literal one-to-one operator mapping is NOT required
requirements.gap: A concrete classical engineering-dimension filtration is defined and closed under addition and bounded-degree multiplication. No corresponding filtered quantum operator spaces or renormalized mixing/identification have been defined.

requirements.description: Short-distance correlation functions agree with asymptotic freedom and perturbative renormalization
requirements.gap: Smeared vacuum n-point functions are now computed directly from QFT field words and the same vacuum. No short-distance scaling limits, asymptotic-freedom estimates, stress tensor or prescribed OPE singularities are proved or formalized.

requirements.description: Existence of stress-energy tensor predicted by the renormalized theory
requirements.gap: No stress-tensor operator or requisite identities are encoded.

requirements.description: Operator product expansion with singularities prescribed by asymptotic freedom
requirements.gap: No fixed OPE coefficients, prescribed singular terms, or asymptotic remainder estimates are encoded.

requirements.description: Nontrivial quantum Yang–Mills theory, excluding free/empty substitutes
requirements.gap: No nontriviality predicate justified for pure Yang–Mills; QFT-and-gap would admit free massive theories.

requirements.description: Positive Hamiltonian spectrum with zero vacuum, Δ > 0, and finite supremum mass m
requirements.gap: Gap is defined from an unbounded Hamiltonian's spectrum, but no existence proof for a YM-identified theory.

requirements.description: Existence of such a nontrivial, identified, gapped theory for every compact simple G
requirements.gap: The groupwise QFT-only shadow and unlinked G-dependent finite gauge invariants are formally provably insufficient. Actual quantum Yang--Mills identification for every compact simple G is not encoded or proved.

outside_required_claim.description: Quark confinement and chiral symmetry breaking in QCD are contextual motivations, not conditions of the pure Yang–Mills Millennium theorem.
Isolated one-particle eigenstates, confinement, extensions to other fields and manifolds are labelled extensions, not additional proof obligations.
A finite-volume regulator or constructive approximation is a possible proof method, not an independently sufficient endpoint.
